Field notes · No. 5

A shelf for movies that mess with you

DJ, founderNovember 6, 20262 min read

Every other Friday a few of us do a movie night, usually at someone’s apartment, sometimes at the IFC Center if it’s showing something worth the line. We have one rule: the movie has to mess with you a little.

For years the list of what to watch lived in a Notes file. It was fine as a list. It was useless as a memory. Nobody could remember why Shutter Island was on it, or whether we’d already decided Gone Girl counted.

So I made a collection board called Mind-benders and pasted the links one by one.

The posters did most of the work. A wall of posters says “what are we in the mood for” in a way a list never does. I circled the two Nolan movies in a region, because at least once a month somebody says “something Nolan” and means one of those two.

The part I didn’t expect was the notes. After we rewatched Inception, the argument about the ending went on until 1 a.m., and nobody won. So I typed it onto the board: “Inception’s ending: did the top fall?” I drew an arrow to the poster and labeled it “Watch again.”

Now the board is half shelf, half group memory. New people get added to the movie night and I just send them a screenshot. They see what we’ve watched and what we fought about.

You don’t need ratings out of ten. You need the thing itself and a few notes in your own words.

If you collect anything at all, try it as a board. Paste a few things and circle the ones that belong together. Then write down the argument you’re still having about one of them.
